named.name: Rosenmund reduction
named.cond: H2 gas, Pd catalyst poisoned with BaSO4 (or S/quinoline), in xylene
named.tip: Poisoned Pd is essential to stop reduction at the aldehyde stage; forgetting BaSO4 poisoning is a common mistake.

named.name: Etard reaction
named.cond: Chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) in CS2/CCl4, then hydrolysis with water
named.tip: Used to convert toluene directly to benzaldehyde; examiners ask for both steps - chromyl chloride addition then hydrolysis.

named.name: Stephen reaction
named.cond: SnCl2 and HCl gas, followed by hydrolysis
named.tip: Converts nitriles to aldehydes; mention the imine (aldimine) salt intermediate before hydrolysis.

named.name: Nucleophilic addition of HCN (cyanohydrin formation)
named.cond: Dilute base (KOH/KCN) as catalyst, low temperature
named.tip: Product is called a cyanohydrin; state that reaction is nucleophilic addition at polar C=O carbon.

named.name: Aldol condensation
named.cond: Dilute NaOH (cold) for aldol, then heat for dehydration
named.tip: Must have alpha-hydrogen; show both the aldol (beta-hydroxy aldehyde) and the final crotonaldehyde after dehydration.

named.name: Cannizzaro reaction
named.cond: Concentrated NaOH/KOH, aldehyde must have NO alpha-hydrogen
named.tip: Disproportionation: one molecule reduced to alcohol, other oxidised to carboxylate salt; only non-alpha-H aldehydes (HCHO, C6H5CHO) undergo this.

named.name: Tollens' test
named.cond: Ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' reagent), warm gently
named.tip: Bright silver mirror confirms aldehyde; ketones give no reaction - a frequently asked distinguishing test.

named.name: Fehling's test
named.cond: Fehling's solution (alkaline CuSO4 with sodium potassium tartrate), heat
named.tip: Brick-red Cu2O precipitate confirms aliphatic aldehyde; aromatic aldehydes (benzaldehyde) give negative Fehling's test.

named.name: Iodoform test
named.cond: I2 and NaOH (or I2/KI with Na2CO3)
named.tip: Positive for methyl ketones, ethanol and acetaldehyde (CH3-CH(OH)- or CH3-CO- pattern); yellow CHI3 precipitate is the identifying result.

named.name: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction
named.cond: Cl2 or Br2 with catalytic red phosphorus
named.tip: Halogenation occurs only at the alpha-carbon and only if an alpha-hydrogen is present; name the catalyst (red P) for full marks.

steps: step 1: CH3CH2OH + PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) -> CH3CHO (mild/controlled oxidation stops at aldehyde)

conversions.q: Convert ethanoic acid (acetic acid) to ethanal (HSC style)
steps: step 1: CH3COOH + reduce to CH3CH2OH is not direct; instead CH3COOH -> CH3COCl using PCl5/SOCl2
step 2: CH3COCl + H2/Pd-BaSO4 (Rosenmund reduction) -> CH3CHO + HCl

conversions.q: Convert benzene to benzaldehyde using the Etard reaction route (HSC style)
steps: step 1: C6H6 + CH3Cl/anhyd. AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) -> C6H5CH3 (toluene)
step 2: C6H5CH3 + CrO2Cl2 (chromyl chloride) in CS2 -> chromium complex, then hydrolyse with water -> C6H5CHO (Etard reaction)

conversions.q: Convert methyl cyanide (acetonitrile) to ethanal using the Stephen reaction (HSC style)
steps: step 1: CH3CN + SnCl2/HCl (gas) -> CH3CH=NH.HCl (aldimine hydrochloride, Stephen reaction)

conversions.q: Convert ethanal to ethanoic acid (HSC style)
steps: step 1: CH3CHO + KMnO4 (acidic/alkaline, strong oxidant) -> CH3COOH (oxidation of aldehyde to acid)

conversions.q: Convert methanal (formaldehyde) to methanol and sodium formate (HSC style, Cannizzaro)
steps: step 1: 2 HCHO + conc. NaOH (Cannizzaro reaction, HCHO has no alpha-H) -> CH3OH + HCOONa (disproportionation: one reduced to alcohol, one oxidised to salt)

conversions.q: Convert propanone (acetone) to mesityl oxide via aldol-type condensation and dehydration (HSC style)
steps: step 1: 2 CH3COCH3 + dil. NaOH (aldol condensation, ketone alpha-H) -> (CH3)2C(OH)-CH2-CO-CH3 (diacetone alcohol)
step 2: (CH3)2C(OH)-CH2-CO-CH3 + heat (-H2O, dehydration) -> (CH3)2C=CH-CO-CH3 (mesityl oxide, an alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone)
conversions.ans: 2 CH3COCH3 --dil. NaOH--> diacetone alcohol --heat, -H2O--> mesityl oxide

conversions.q: Convert acetic acid to glycine (aminoacetic acid) via chloroacetic acid using the HVZ reaction (HSC style)
steps: step 1: CH3COOH + Cl2/red P (HVZ reaction) -> ClCH2COOH + HCl
step 2: ClCH2COOH + NH3 (excess, nucleophilic substitution) -> NH2CH2COOH (glycine) + HCl
